own_solution.law: Conservation of momentum and kinetic energy gives v1f = ((m1-m2)u1 + 2m2u2)/(m1+m2). Thus the base answer is ((3-2)6 + 2(2)(1))/5 = +2 m/s. With an attached block of mass q, replace m1 by 3+q, giving v1f = (10+6q)/(5+q).
assumptions: The given velocities apply immediately before the collision.
There is no external impulse along the track during the collision.
A rigidly attached block moves with its cart and contributes to its collision mass.
The earlier-run block is absent during the stated collision.
The third cart does not interact with the colliding carts.

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: T1828 and T2689 replace the numerical mass and unit with 'small', violating the review instructions' requirement that variants concerning the same quantity preserve its number and unit, even though the authors identify these omissions as intentional controls.
defect_reasons.other: The description calls the collision 'head-on' while explicitly specifying motion in the same direction, creating a minor terminological inconsistency.

notes: All physical classifications, dependency claims, dimensions and certified numerical answers agree with my pass-1 solution. For either relevant sentence, q = 0.7, 1.3 and 2.2 kg gives respectively +2.4912280702, +2.8253968254 and +3.2222222222 m/s; the reported rounding is adequate. All disconnected sentences leave the answer at +2 m/s. The explicitly named minimal pairs T180A/T8516 and TFB40/T9B35 preserve the stated mass and unit and change only the intended temporal or object attachment. Pass 2 explains that T1828 and T2689 deliberately omit numerals; this clarifies their design but does not satisfy the supplied blanket requirement that quantity variants retain the same number and unit, so I retain that pass-1 defect. The invalid verdict concerns this rendering requirement, not the collision solution. The explicit same-direction velocities resolve the intended calculation despite the term 'head-on'.
